clue.text: Unsteadily move coach around American railway system

annotationWithheld.why: Unsteadily move coach around American railway system (6): SWAY round SUB (coach, BUS, turned around) gives SSUBWAY, one S too many; the only parse needs the S to do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Unsteadily move coach around American railway system

clue.text: Type of oil carried by ship as far as possible

indicators.note: 'possible' says this group of letters could form a different word

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Oil carried as far as a ship can go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges SS with AS FAR AS; 'carried by' is surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil of sassafras is distilled from the root bark of a North American tree of the laurel family.

clue.text: Surreptitiously installing Mike? That's bothersome

definitions.meaning: secretly fitting a mike, a microphone, to eavesdrop
irritating or pestering, as in 'what's annoying you?'

explanation.surface: A spy secretly plants a microphone, which proves a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is a hidden listening device, and to bug someone is to annoy them.

clue.text: Carrier of blood — two types needed at car crash

parts.note: A and O are blood groups
RTA stands for road traffic accident

explanation.surface: At a car crash two blood groups are needed for transfusion.
explanation.walkthrough: RTA, for road traffic accident, is a British abbreviation for a car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery taking blood out of the heart.

clue.text: Fuel to burn in cleaner state when oxygen is injected

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, a charwoman

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so the oxygen symbol is placed within the state abbreviation

parts.note: CAL is a short form of California, an American state
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Advice on getting fuel to burn cleanly by feeding it more oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is injected' puts O inside CAL to make COAL. A char is British slang for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal is a carbon fuel made by heating wood, burned in barbecues and braziers.

clue.text: Defeat, also, Chinese gangs with great effort

parts.note: to hammer is to beat heavily
and means also, in addition
tongs are Chinese secret societies or gangs

explanation.surface: A struggle to defeat Chinese gangs with great effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means vigorously, energetically, like a blacksmith at work.

clue.text: One could help dry country — Iran, possibly?

definitions.text: One could help dry country — Iran, possibly?

parts.words: One could help dry country — Iran, possibly?
parts.note: someone who brings rain to a parched land; also, the four letters of Iran rearranged make rain, so Iran could produce it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a parched country like Iran could be helped.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: shuffle IRAN and you make RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainmaker claims to bring rain by magic or cloud-seeding, so helps parched land.

clue.text: For example, first book that could be the making of a clergyman

definitions.meaning: first, second and third are numbers of position in a series

definitions.text: book that could be the making of a clergyman
definitions.meaning: a service book for ordaining priests and deacons

explanation.surface: First, perhaps, a book that may turn a man into a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers state position; an ordinal is also the book of rites for ordination.

clue.text: Losing water from lake, ruined and ultimately dry

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of the word are broken up and reset
ultimately points to the last letter of the word dry

explanation.surface: A lake is ruined by losing its water and ending up dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges LAKE to LEAK and 'ultimately' adds the last letter of 'dry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaky vessel lets liquid escape through holes.

clue.text: Experienced politician and church official one found in US?

parts.note: an elder holds office in a Presbyterian church
read as a man of the States, a person found in America

explanation.surface: Describing a politician who is also a church official in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the joke reading: a statesman as a 'States man', someone in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder statesman is a senior politician respected for long experience.

clue.text: Sweet sort of dancing fairy

definitions.meaning: a small sugared confection eaten as a treat
the ballet fairy in The Nutcracker is named after this treat

explanation.surface: A charming description of a dainty ballet fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sugar Plum Fairy dances in Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugarplum is a small round sugared confection, and the Nutcracker's fairy bears that name.

clue.text: In Sind I appreciate you will no longer be here

definitions.text: you will no longer be here

indicators.note: the letters sit in the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A visitor to Sind is told that the province has changed hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Sind' through 'I' into 'appreciate'. Sind became part of Pakistan in 1947, so a visitor there is no longer in this country.
explanation.definitionFit: Since partition the province of Sind lies in Pakistan, outside the republic of Delhi.

clue.text: Inner personality I'm showing in articles

indicators.note: the contraction is placed inside the pair of articles

parts.note: AN and A are the indefinite articles
I'M written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A psychologist's remark that someone's true self shows in what they write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' supplies two separate words, the two indefinite articles, and the contraction sits between them. 'showing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jung's psychology the anima is the inner self, the soul as distinct from the outward persona.

clue.text: Yet my holding ace gives chance to double profitably

parts.note: even and yet both mean still, as in 'even more'

indicators.note: one word holds another when it is wrapped round it, so the letters of my enclose the number

parts.note: taken as written
an ace counts as one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A card player holding an ace sees the chance to double the stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yet' and 'even' are interchangeable in 'yet more' and 'even more'. Evens is betting talk for odds that return double the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet at evens pays back the stake plus an equal sum, doubling the punter's outlay.

clue.text: Chap brought in to reanimate zoo site

indicators.note: the man is brought into the middle of the other word, inside its letters

parts.note: to re-spark is to bring life back, to revive
a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: A keeper is hired to bring a tired zoo back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zoo site' is fair because London Zoo stands in Regent's Park in north London; 're-spark' is coined for the clue as bringing back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Zoo lies within this royal park, so the park is where the zoo is found.

clue.text: Type of non-standard story written up

parts.note: non means not, and par is the standard

indicators.note: in a down clue written up means put upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A tall tale of an odd kind gets printed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns LIE to EIL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil was a size of printing type, about six points, so it names a type size.

clue.text: The French kiss, showing loose morality

parts.note: la is French for 'the' before a feminine noun
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A French kiss is taken as a sign of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French kiss' looks like the familiar phrase; it splits into LA and X.
explanation.definitionFit: Lax means slack or careless, so lax morals are loose ones.

clue.text: Source of music that has a striking effect on bars

definitions.text: Source of music that has a striking effect on bars

parts.words: Source of music that has a striking effect on bars
parts.note: musical bars suggest time signatures, but here the bars are wooden ones played by hitting them

explanation.surface: Music with a dramatic effect on a pub or on bars of a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' seems to mean bars of music; it means the wooden slats struck with mallets.
explanation.definitionFit: This percussion instrument has wooden bars hit with hammers to make notes.

clue.text: This standardly indicates respect, beginning letters

definitions.text: This standardly indicates respect, beginning letters

indicators.note: beginning letters are the first letters of the three words standardly, indicates and respect

explanation.surface: A note that a certain form of address conventionally signals respect.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'standardly indicates respect' spell the word, and the whole clue describes it: the polite address starts many formal letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the standard respectful form of address to a man and the usual opening of a formal letter.

clue.text: Give new place to that woman over the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: her refers to a woman
the Ouse is a river in England, the name of several English rivers

explanation.surface: A woman is moved to a home across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns HER to REH. The Ouse is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehouse is to provide someone with a different home.

clue.text: Extremely conservative characters in NE heartland

indicators.note: the characters in the phrase, its letters, are taken and rearranged to make a new word

explanation.surface: A remark that the north-east heartland is full of reactionary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in' says to take the letters of NE HEARTLAND and rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a Neanderthal means they are hopelessly old-fashioned and reactionary, like a caveman.

clue.text: Thumping success, sound as a bell

parts.note: a hit is a success, a smash
ting is the light ringing sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: A big success, as sound as a bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy; it is the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumping and striking are both blows dealt to someone.

clue.text: Call for effort that can help one cat, for example

definitions.text: Call for effort that can help one cat, for example

parts.words: Call for effort that can help one cat, for example
parts.note: a sailors' chant when hauling together; 'cat' is slang for vomiting, so the chant's middle word also means to throw up

explanation.surface: A shout of encouragement that might help someone deal with a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: To cat is British slang for to vomit, which is also to heave, so the sailors' hauling cry could help one heave.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the rhythmic shout sailors gave while hauling ropes, a call to pull together.

clue.text: Change partner at end of long, long time

indicators.note: in bridge North partners South, so the final compass letter is swapped for its partner

parts.note: to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: Swapping a partner after a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South are partners, so 'Change partner at end of' swaps the N at the end of YEARN for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Years means a great while, as in 'I haven't seen her in ages'.

clue.text: Wounded, physically or emotionally

parts.note: the phrase can mean slashed in body or upset in feelings

explanation.surface: A description of someone hurt in body or spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means lacerated, and figuratively distressed, as in 'she was badly upset by the news'.

clue.text: Said to improve social situation in region

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard rather than read, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to climb is to rise socially, as a social climber does

explanation.surface: Someone tries to better their social standing in a particular area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' tells you to use a word that sounds like CLIMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A clime is a climate or a part of the world, as in 'sunnier climes'.

clue.text: A blue that is unknown in a river

indicators.note: the unknown letter is placed inside the two-part container

parts.note: taken as written
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A colour description: a river of uncertain identity, coloured blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts Z inside A + URE. The Ure is a river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is the bright blue of a clear sky, one shade of that colour.

clue.text: Grandee will be seen if a coming can be arranged

indicators.note: a set of letters that can be arranged may be put into a new order

explanation.surface: A great man will appear if his arrival is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be arranged' says the letters of IF A COMING are to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifico was a Venetian magnate, hence any great personage or nobleman.

clue.text: Business activity nets millions, giving suspicion of corruption?

indicators.note: to net is to catch inside a mesh, so one word encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: selling is the trading that businesses do
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A firm's trade brings in millions, raising suspicions of corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nets' puts M inside SELLING. The question mark marks a looser definition: something smelling of corruption hints at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that reeks or stinks of something suggests it, as a deal may stink of graft.

clue.text: Going extremely suitable for horse?

parts.note: the outside letters of 'going' are two Gs, each letter spelt out as its name

explanation.surface: Asking whether the ground conditions are especially suited to a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' looks like racing's word for the ground; its first and last letters are G and G, written out as names of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee-gee is a childish or jokey word for a horse.
